data.title: "Subtle changes pointing to consumer fatigue" a challenge for fast-fashion retailers, expert says
data.description: A federation of European textile associations called Tuesday for an import fee of 10 euros on fashion imports, the latest effort to stem the flood of ultra-cheap competition mainly from China. Speaking with FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney, Dr Sheng Lu, Professor at the Department of Fashion and Apparel Studies at the University of Delaware, says that it remains to be seen just "to what extent such measures would push groups like Shein to change their business model", adding that fast-fashion retailers may have to start to contend with "consumer fatigue".

data.title: Germany blames Russia for airport drone incident, hits back with sanctions
data.description: Germany on Tuesday blamed Russia for an attempted "hybrid attack" involving an explosive-laden drone at a strategic airport last month and announced diplomatic counter-measures. The European Union expressed "full solidarity" with Germany, NATO assured that it would defend its members and countries including Britain, Estonia and Poland offered strong backing. Germany will close Russia's consulate in the former capital Bonn later this month, and cancel the contract for the Russian House, a cultural centre in Berlin, said Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul. FRANCE 24's Carys Garland reports.

data.title: The year of Domhnall Gleeson: ‘No one talks about actors’ dedication. But I had a perm for five months!’
data.description: He started in the Harry Potter films and has since become ubiquitous, playing every type of character: romcom leads, evil villains, comical idiots. He even starred in a Taylor Swift video. So how does he stay so under the radar? Domhnall Gleeson has got so much new stuff coming up, someone recently joked that this was the “summer of Domhnall”. Now the phrase is all over the internet, and Gleeson is mortified: “The worry is that somebody will say this to me now thinking that I believe it.” He doesn’t know where it came from – possibly his co-star Gayle Rankin on his new movie The Incomer. “It’s certainly not something I’m trying to push … but it would be great if it could be the headline.” He’s in a good mood when we meet at a London hotel on a hot afternoon. You could say he’s good at interviews – charming, funny, garrulous, the perfect chatshow guest. He could just be acting , admittedly, but he seems to be a genuinely good-natured, grounded sort of guy. Continue reading...

data.title: A moment that changed me: I had a panic attack on public transport – and it led me to a horrifying secret
data.description: For a decade I lived with a fear so bad that I once tried to climb out of a tube carriage while it was in motion. Then a hypnotherapist told me to ask my parents one very important question In 2000, I had been living in London for just over a decade and working at EMI Records for five years. I had moved to Brixton from Surrey – where space and peace were generally abundant – in the late 80s, and I’d noticed I was becoming increasingly anxious and claustrophobic, particularly on public transport. As things got progressively worse, I had a string of distressing panic attacks. Every time, it felt like the world around me was closing in. Then, in July 2003, during my daily commute between Brixton and the South Bank, I had a panic attack so intense I tried to climb out of the tube carriage doors. Thankfully, other passengers held me back until we arrived at the next platform – but I knew the problem was no longer something I could ignore. Continue reading...

data.title: The shadow of the AfD hangs over German democracy – but I still have faith in my adopted country | John Kampfner
data.description: As I celebrate five years of citizenship, the far right is poised to take control in Saxony-Anhalt. Courage is needed to defeat it Two events take place in coming days that will affect my relationship with Germany. One, which will be splashed across the media, is dark and forbidding. The other, which will pass unnoticed except by me and my close family, should have brought me joy. Now that feeling is tempered with confusion. On 6 September, voters in the small eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt are expected to give Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) a resounding victory. If the arithmetic falls in a certain way, a German far-right party could assume power for the first time since the Nazis. John Kampfner is a Berlin-based author and broadcaster. His latest book, Braver New World , is published by Atlantic Continue reading...

data.title: HRH Helch: the graffiti artist who left an indelible mark on high-rise Britain
data.description: He upset Queen Elizabeth II, defied the developers and had to scrap for every inch of graffiti space in a gentrified, urban landscape • Prolific UK graffiti artist Helch dies You know you’ve made an impact when the headlines upon your death are filled with words like “iconic”, “infamous”, “world class” and “upset Queen Elizabeth II”. By that measure, graffiti supremo Helch made a pretty serious mark on the world. He died this week , leaving behind a country pockmarked by his tag, a giant towering HELCH, though sometimes reduced to just a simple upper-case H. It was on railway bridges and motorway overpasses, on derelict buildings and decrepit high rises. From Bristol to London, Helch was everywhere. He was even on a railway viaduct on the way to Windsor Castle, in 60ft high white letters, “ruining” the view of poor old Elizabeth’s home and apparently leaving our late monarch in an absolute rage. Continue reading...

data.title: UK must end all trade with Israel, says co-founder of BDS movement
data.description: Exclusive: sanctions against ministers and settler groups are ‘smoke and mirrors cop-out’ says Omar Barghouti Britain’s legal and ethical obligation to stop a genocide in Gaza requires it to take bigger steps than halting trade with illegal Israeli settlements or imposing further sanctions, Omar Barghouti, the co-founder of the Boycott, Divestment, Sanctions (BDS) movement has said. He described sanctions against individual settler groups or extremist ministers as a “smoke and mirrors cop-out and distraction” from the UK’s legal obligation under international law to end all support for Israel, including arms exports, trade deals and academic relations that “may directly or indirectly enable Israel’s illegal occupation” of Gaza, the West Bank and East Jerusalem. Continue reading...

data.description: But scientists say the world could get back to 1.5C through deep, rapid emissions cuts and removing carbon from the atmosphere Global heating will reach at least 1.8C under even the most optimistic future, well beyond the Paris agreement goal of 1.5C, according to a UN report that warns every fraction of temperature rise intensifies destructive extreme weather, glacier melt, ecosystem loss, and island and coastal city submersion. The report by the Nairobi-based UN Environment Programme confirmed overshooting the 1.5C goal inscribed in the landmark Paris agreement of 2015 was now “unavoidable” and, despite some progress in addressing the human-caused climate crisis driven by burning fossil fuels, likely in the next few years. data.title: Edouard Balladur obituary
data.description: French prime minister beaten to the presidency by his former ally Jacques Chirac at the 1995 election For many months before the 1995 French presidential election, Édouard Balladur, the incumbent prime minister, seemed certain of victory. Opinion polls consistently gave him a lead over his conservative rival Jacques Chirac , and the main leftwing candidate. But, as other politicians have discovered, polls can be misleading and voters change their minds. When the ballot papers were counted it was Chirac who won and succeeded François Mitterrand as president. The defeat of Balladur, who has died aged 97, was due partly to his lack of appeal to young voters, a consequence of his public image which, somewhat unfairly, was that of an aloof aristocrat. When he first became a minister, the satirical weekly newspaper Le Canard Enchaîné dubbed him “his courteous self-importance” and Le Monde’s cartoonist Plantu depicted him as a bewigged 18th-century nobleman being carried around in a sedan chair. His manner and style – three-piece English tailored suits, dislike (figuratively and literally) of getting his hands dirty and obvious distaste for close personal contact – did not play well in the context of a presidential contest. Continue reading...

data.title: The Gentlemen season two review – these geezers in tweed are irritating, stupid and extremely funny
data.description: Guy Ritchie’s crime caper is back with the usual hijinks, swearing and men shaking their fists. But its ridiculousness is strangely comforting – and Theo James’s beefcake Eddie is so bland that he is fascinating to observe He lives in a house, a very big house in the country. He has pectorals the size of Bentleys and wears plus-fours so voluminous they could accommodate his fleet of gundogs and still provide room for snarling groundskeeper Geoff (“I would do anyfink for you an’ this famlee”). And yet! Edward “Eddie” Horniman, 13th Duke of Halstead (Theo James), is sad. And aggrieved. A moment’s silence, please, as this powerful hunk pontificates on the unbearable lightness of being the millionaire protagonist in Guy Ritchie’s The Gentlemen. “Four hundred years ago, this estate spread out as far as the eye could see,” he tells Geoff (Vinnie Jones) as the camera swoops over his verdant playpen, a lavish patchwork of abundant hedges and cap-doffing deer. “But it’s been diminished. Year after year. Generation after generation. First came the apologies, then came the shame, then came the contraction. I want it back, Geoff,” he growls, hexagonal jaw stiff with emotion. “I want it all back!” Continue reading...

data.title: The Bridge by Colm Tóibín review – betrayal and survival in the High Pyrenees
data.description: Deep sorrow mingles with illicit desire in this potent novella, the follow-up to a 2006 story about an isolated family in the Catalan mountains Twenty years ago, Colm Tóibín published a steadily desolating novella set in the high villages of the Catalan Pyrenees. A woman walks out of her house and her life, starts along the mountain road and disappears in the snow. Her son Miquel, failing to find her body, waits through the dark months for the thaw. A Long Winter, which appeared in a standalone volume and then as the final story in the 2006 collection Mothers and Sons, followed Miquel through dramatically extreme circumstances and patient endurance. It was told with the most restrained prose ever likely to be employed for a son’s view of vultures circling a corpse. Now, in The Bridge, a single year has passed in Miquel’s life and he is eking out an existence with his hurtful, unyielding father. The sheep are grazing their high summer pastures; a side hustle smuggling contraband brings in a little much-needed cash. In the bare conditions of the lonely farm, any warmth of feeling is a kind of contraband smuggled in by night; love between men is doubly illicit. The grave tenderness that grows between Miquel and his father’s maltreated servant Manolo gives The Bridge its emotional centre. These young men salve the emptiness with a few quiet words and touches. We sense their youthful beauty and resilience, their suppleness in a place of fixity. Continue reading...

data.title: Andy Burnham has already made a mistake that will cost him his premiership: he lost his nerve over political donations | George Monbiot
data.description: Being subservient to the interests of the wealthy now means that his hands are tied, and he will be unable to tackle Britain’s most pressing issues Damn the electorate. They’re so impatient . No sooner do they get a new leader than they want another one. Those ingrates are already starting to grumble about Andy Burnham. Maybe the country is becoming ungovernable . Perhaps it’s social media . Or a consumerist culture, always picking the next shiny thing. Perhaps we’re addicted to drama . As we’re on our sixth prime minister in 10 years, and as similar levels of discontent surface in many other countries, these claims are recited across the media. What’s wrong with us? Yet our disgruntlement is entirely rational. We give up so quickly on our prime ministers because they give up so quickly on us. Though it may involve different issues, it is always the same betrayal: the public interest is sacrificed for the sake of a tiny number of immensely wealthy people. And it tends to happen almost immediately. George Monbiot is a Guardian columnist Continue reading...

data.title: It’s not easy to show my scars. But I am proud to break the deadly silence around breast cancer in Nigeria | Gloria Chinyere Okwu
data.description: I was told to keep my diagnosis private but I am determined to show the reality of breast cancer and reject the stigma that prevents women seeking treatment ‘Madam, this looks like breast cancer, and if it is, we will chop off your breast.” That was how the doctor welcomed me into the chaotic world of cancer in 2017 when I was 32 years old. He had his back to me, but kept on talking, peering into the specimen bottle. For a moment, I could no longer hear him. I thought of my three children, the university degree I had just bagged and the future I had envisaged. If I was going to die, what was the point of it all? I had invested everything I had to obtain that degree, subjecting my children to days of absence while I spent my nights in the university library. Continue reading...

data.title: Olivia Rodrigo is standing up for the vulnerable. I wish Taylor Swift would do the same | Arwa Mahdawi
data.description: This weekend, Rodrigo raised millions for charities that benefit women and girls, and she has previously been vocal about Gaza and Ice. With free speech increasingly under threat, her peers should take note Donald Trump, the 80-year-old president of the United States, spent his weekend whining about a lake and posting memes of Donald’s Ducks . While he was busy with his ducks, Olivia Rodrigo, a 23-year-old pop star, spent her weekend trying to Make America Somewhat Decent Again. On Saturday, Rodrigo hosted the inaugural Daisy Chain Fields festival , bringing together female artists to raise money for women-focused non-profits which have had their funding slashed by the Trump administration. The festival raised $10m (£7.4m) which Melinda French Gates matched, bringing the total to $20m. In a perfect world a singer holding a benefit concert for feminist charities wouldn’t be radical stuff. But we don’t live in a perfect world, do we? We live in hell. Trump has successfully bullied US institutions into doing his bidding. Universities have defunded diversity, equity and inclusion programmes, many media outlets have kowtowed to the US’s self-styled king and tech CEOs have jumped into bed with him. Women’s rights are going backwards globally and our civil liberties are under attack. Continue reading...

data.title: The Guardian view on loneliness: the decline in friendship leaves gen Z exposed | Editorial
data.description: Problems with housing, jobs and technology have dented young people’s confidence in the future and each other Hope, Raye told a crowd at Reading festival on Saturday, was the theme of a set inspired by her second album . Having established through a show of hands that most of the audience had just done their GCSEs, and after recounting her own rocky road to stardom, the 28-year-old singer led a series of upbeat chants of “it’s gonna be all right”. For anyone who thinks adolescence ought to be a time of optimism, it was a charming spectacle. But a new report from the Institute for Public Policy Research thinktank paints a much gloomier picture. Building on existing evidence of declining wellbeing, such as Alan Milburn’s report on young people who are not in education or work, the IPPR’s researchers found that 11- to 24-year-olds in England (gen Z and older members of gen Alpha) are increasingly lonely . They have fewer friends than young people in the past and are less contented with those they do have. One in 20 say that they have no friends at all. A series of interviews produced worrying evidence of their lack of confidence about the future. Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? data.title: The Guardian view on the global bond shock: Andy Burnham should take note | Editorial
data.description: Japan’s collision with Donald Trump reveals the dilemma facing Britain: economic independence is becoming more necessary – and more tricky to achieve “In the midst of every crisis lies great opportunity” is an aphorism attributed to Albert Einstein . It seems to be taken to heart by this White House. A global bond sell-off sparked by an inflationary shock emanating from the Gulf sees Donald Trump seeking to restrict plans by Japan – a longtime ally – to reduce dependence on an international system America dominates. Japan, a successful exporter, has long done things its own way. For years Tokyo saw off the bond vigilantes despite running enormous deficits and a huge national debt. It demonstrated how a central bank could fund public spending and keep interest rates low if it wanted to. This economic model was refined by Shinzo Abe, Japan’s longest-serving prime minister. However, this week the US treasury secretary, Scott Bessent , called time on Abenomics as his price for US help in stabilising Japan’s currency. Japan’s Sanae Takaichi, he indicated, should shrink her $2tn spending plans and raise rates. Abenomics did not suddenly become financially impossible. It became inconvenient to the issuer of the world’s reserve currency. Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? data.translatedDescription: Japan’s collision with Donald Trump reveals the dilemma facing Britain: economic independence is becoming more necessary – and more tricky to achieve “In the midst of every crisis lies great opportunity” is an aphorism attributed to Albert Einstein . It seems to be taken to heart by this White House. A global bond sell-off sparked by an inflationary shock emanating from the Gulf sees Donald Trump seeking to restrict plans by Japan – a longtime ally – to reduce dependence on an international system America dominates. Japan, a successful exporter, has long done things its own way. For years Tokyo saw off the bond vigilantes despite running enormous deficits and a huge national debt. It demonstrated how a central bank could fund public spending and keep interest rates low if it wanted to. This economic model was refined by Shinzo Abe, Japan’s longest-serving prime minister. However, this week the US treasury secretary, Scott Bessent , called time on Abenomics as his price for US help in stabilising Japan’s currency. Japan’s Sanae Takaichi, he indicated, should shrink her $2tn spending plans and raise rates. Abenomics did not suddenly become financially impossible. It became inconvenient to the issuer of the world’s reserve currency. Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? data.title: Football connects communities but can pull them apart if governed carelessly
data.description: Sport is a space to help youngsters develop character, resilience and confidence, but we need stronger leadership and safer environments to make this happen The fight for the soul of football isn’t just happening in the offices of Uefa and Fifa, it’s taking place on pitches much closer to home. At the weekend games of football for 750 children aged five to six in Scotland were cancelled due to severe behavioural issues within the ironically named “Fun 4s” programme. Seventy-two red cards were handed out in the first week of the season. Accounts describe adults displaying aggression, intimidation and head-butting as if it’s the “wild west”. This isn’t just a Scottish problem. Contacts I speak to in different roles around football confirm and almost accept that “youth football is atrocious”. This should be sounding major alarm bells, for the consequences go way beyond the pitch. The existing disciplinary systems and PR campaigns are not nearly enough to address and change the situation. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘A cheeseburger worked really well’: the secrets behind a record-breaking 152-hour run
data.description: On a diet including plenty of fast food and with virtually no sleep, Australian endurance athlete Phil Gore ran 6.71km every hour for an entire week Being wrenched out of deep sleep by your alarm and forced to leave the comfort of your bed can be a horrible experience at the best of times. To go through that process again and again over the course of one night sounds like a bad dream. But last week, for six days and 15 hours, it was Phil Gore’s reality. It gets worse – or better, depending on your penchant for self-inflicted suffering. Each time ultra-runner Gore was woken he had two minutes to put on his shoes and headtorch before a bell signalled it was time to start his next 6.71km running lap. He had slept for no more than 15 minutes. Pounding the pavement in the dark while the Perth suburb of Forrestdale slept, Gore would return about 40 minutes later and jump straight back into the bed he had set up at the Armadale Soccer Club. Rinse and repeat, all night, then all day (minus the sleep), all week. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘They take the water, the springs dry up’: fear as Guatemalan goldmine plan is revived
data.description: After lying dormant for years, the Era Dorada project in Asunción Mita resumed this year and villagers say history is being repeated, despite promises of change In the community of La Lima in Guatemala , Elda Dinora Ramírez, 58, looks towards a small well at the back of her home. Dusty wooden planks lie across the opening, concealing the faint gleam of water far below. “The well is drying up again,” she says. Ramírez’s home lies less than a mile from Era Dorada – a goldmining project acquired by the Canadian multinational Aura Minerals in January 2025. After years of inactivity, the project was reactivated this year when the Guatemalan government granted Aura a construction licence . Continue reading...

data.title: Britain is OK with public ownership, but only by foreign powers. Why?
data.description: Arthur Downing, author of Power and the People: A History of British Energy, says all-encompassing rapid transition will need a mutualised system Have you ever wondered why it is that most houses in the UK are reliant on gas boilers? Not what’s stopping more people from replacing them with heat pumps, but instead why and how the gas boiler became so ubiquitous in the first place? Arthur Downing, the author of the new book Power and the People: A History of British Energy, can tell you exactly why. “We only have boilers in our houses because of a state-owned enterprise that went into everybody’s home and installed natural gas-suitable appliances at no direct cost,” he says. The nationalised gas industry of the 1940s to the 1980s, which oversaw this huge project, was for three decades one of the “most dynamic, innovative, efficient industries in Britain”, Downing says. Yet few of us would use these terms to describe it as such now. Continue reading...

data.title: Waking Life: Richard Linklater’s genre-defying indie is a kaleidoscopic masterpiece
data.description: Wiley Wiggins plays a man wandering around Austin, Texas, whose reality-bending encounters make him uncertain whether he’s awake or asleep “I’m gonna tell you about a dream I once had,” Richard Linklater – playing himself in his own film Waking Life – tells Wiley Wiggins, playing the film’s unnamed protagonist. “I know when someone says that usually you’re in for a very boring next few minutes, and you might be,” Linklater adds as he hammers away at a pinball machine. “But it sounds like … what else you gonna do, right?” On paper, that’s the premise – and, if you’re cynical, the central dilemma – of Linklater’s 2001 genre-defying indie masterpiece. Wiggins plays a man wandering around Austin, Texas, who is uncertain whether he’s awake or asleep. He may be stuck in a dream, unable to wake up – or reality might just be this weird. data.description: From ceramic goblin feet to furry disembodied legs, Korean-Chinese artist Woo Jin Joo is using London junk to inject the art world with a spirit of playfulness Woo Jin Joo’s studio is full of magic. Ceramic green goblin feet line the windowsill, disembodied furry legs jut out of one white wall and, on the table behind where the Korean-Chinese artist sits drinking tea, a headless being dressed in a black coat squats, arms aloft in warning. There are also neat racks of colourful thread next to a freehand embroidery machine, the source of this supernatural horde. This is where Joo creates much of her art – surface embroideries and sculptural 3D creatures inspired by Korean myth, philosophy and the relationship between humans and the natural world. data.title: Late Fame review – Willem Dafoe superb as ever as twilight-years bohemian getting a second chance
data.description: Samy Burch’s adaptation of an Arthur Schnitzler novella sees Dafoe’s ageing poet embraced by a younger cohort of capricious hipsters. It’s smart, literate and affecting There’s a marvellous tenderness and generosity to this elegant tale of autumnal regret; an intimate movie acted with effortless grace by Willem Dafoe. In fact, this is yet another of his almost numberless performances of intelligence and self-possession. Screenwriter Samy Burch has adapted a novella by Arthur Schnitzler, which has been directed by critic turned film-maker Kent Jones (who in 2015 made Hitchcock/Truffaut , a documentary that I very much admired). Their movie finds a new variation on the Schnitzlerian theme of life’s lost opportunities for love, lust and success, and how, as mortality’s shadow closes in, one might be tempted to risk everything for a last chance at worldly triumph. The main character here is a distant cousin – though a wiser cousin – to the doctor in Schnitzler’s Traumnovelle or Dream Story, filmed by Kubrick as Eyes Wide Shut. Dafoe plays Ed Saxberger, an old guy in New York who works in the post office, sorting mail, perhaps without the means to retire, living solo in a small but book-filled room in a humble walkup, drinking and playing pool with his buddies in the evening. One day, Saxberger is astonished to be accosted by a dandyish young hipster outside his apartment building; this is Meyers (played by Edmund Donovan), who knows something about Saxberger that nobody else does. Saxberger was once a talented young poet in the 70s New York bohemian scene and Meyers has found his long since out-of-print volume of poems, entitled Way Past Go. He declares Saxberger a neglected genius that he, and his similarly callow and excitable literary friends, are going to take up. Continue reading...

data.title: Turning Point: Generation 9/11 review – nothing about that day has lost its power to shock or harrow the soul
data.description: The attacks changed the world as we know it – and now, 25 years on, this heartbreaking Netflix film shares 9/11 recordings and memories from the bereaved that stop time in its tracks It is 25 years since two planes, sent by Osama bin Laden as the head of the terrorist organisation al-Qaida, flew into the North and South Towers that comprised the World Trade Center, killing almost 3,000 people and changing the world as we know it. I’m old enough to remember the day itself – I was a trainee lawyer in London and we watched the news unfold on a conference room television – which means I am also old enough to remember the world before it. But a quarter of a century on, it is taught in schools as a historical event. Can you believe it? No, because if you experience such a convulsive moment – even at the distance of being a television viewer in a different country – time bends around it and normal chronology becomes meaningless ever after. But that is only our perspective. Continue reading...

data.title: The Runner review – Gal Gadot stumbles through derivative high-speed, low-rent thriller
data.description: A string of London locations can’t save Amazon’s overly familiar B-movie dragged down by another ineffective performance by the Wonder Woman star We’re propelled on to an extremely familiar journey in Amazon’s quickie action thriller The Runner, both in reheated premise and strategic aim. The film is yet another example of a real-time assassination nightmare as an ordinary citizen is placed in an extraordinary situation, forced to do something terrible by someone terrible. Think Johnny Depp in Nick of Time, Rachel McAdams in Red Eye, Shia LaBeouf in Eagle Eye, or more recently, Taron Egerton in Carry-On and Meghann Fahy in Drop , with technology increasingly a key component. We’re also faced with what’s another strained attempt to turn Gal Gadot into a movie star, a mission that’s proved close to impossible after she broke out in Wonder Woman. Her streaming vehicles, like Red Notice and Heart of Stone , might have proved easy at-home hits (the latter was also surprisingly entertaining), but on the big screen, playing both a Disney villain and an Agatha Christie victim proved to be of little interest to audiences, who chose meme-ing her worst moments over turning up to see them. An action-first film like The Runner, disposable and undemanding, might seem like the safest place for Gadot’s rather limited skill set, but even with a role that asks more of her physically than emotionally, it’s still a rather awkward stretch. Luckily, she’s paired with real on-the-ground London locations, from Kentish Town to Somerset House, the city proving to be a scene-stealing co-star. Gadot plays Maia, a single mother and lawyer, who says goodbye to her diabetic son at school and starts her run to work (surely her son’s diabetes will not become an important part of the plot, right? ). But her day is soon interrupted by a nefarious “freelancer” working for a local crime boss, voiced by Damian Lewis. He has kidnapped her son and hacked his insulin dispenser, forcing him into a hypoglycemic coma, his life hanging in the balance until Maia agrees to murder a key witness she was supposed to be representing in court that morning. The film’s slight novelty is that Maia must run five miles to the hotel where he’s staying within an hour, no interruptions allowed. The slight 2026 update is that, in what’s increasingly becoming a lazy crutch for screenwriters, AI is an important weapon. Continue reading...

data.title: Hungry review – hippo horror sees multi-ton mammal run amok among bayou boat-trippers
data.description: A group of thinly drawn characters on a Louisiana tour fight for survival against a rampaging vegetarian This animal-attack horror plugs a gap with beasties – hippopotamuses – that may be deadly in real life but are hard to take seriously as a threat on screen. As someone says here, they have cute ears. Even the film’s title, evoking the kids’ game Hungry Hungry Hippos, diminishes the menace. That’s perhaps not the tone to set if you’re trying to persuade audiences that fatal consequences are in the offing. And as the script often reminds us, hippos are vegetarian, so hunger isn’t driving these multi-ton mammals to murder. Turns out they’re massively territorial, and especially dangerous when protecting their young. That, or they do just think killing people is fun. The film naturally spends less time worrying about the hippos’ motives and dwells more on the victims, who look pretty doomed given their thin characterisations. This lot certainly weren’t expecting to be attacked by a hippo when they woke up because they are on a bayou tour in Louisiana, where the biggest threats are normally alligators. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘It’s more freaky, more balls to the wall’: how alt-country won over a new generation
data.description: From Waxahatchee and Florry in the US to Brown Horse and Little Grandad in the UK, a wave of young songwriters are reinvigorating the subgenre’s earnest emotion and twang ‘It’s so important to talk about this before it’s gone,” says Francie Medosch, singer, guitarist and songwriter of the band Florry, “because it’s really a flash in the pan.” The flash she means is a brief moment where it feels as though on both sides of the Atlantic, scores of exciting indie bands are playing something that, without slavish copying, has plainly drawn inspiration from alt-country, the music that emerged in the US in the late 1980s and early 90s, when former punks such as Uncle Tupelo – featuring future Wilco co-founder Jeff Tweedy – and the Bottle Rockets picked up picked up fiddles, banjos and acoustic guitars. In the UK, Brown Horse and Vegas Water Taxi have the weeping pedal steel, in the former case tied to something very heartland and in the latter paired with a very English indie sensibility. Westside Cowboy and Little Grandad both borrow from the spiky rootsiness of early Wilco, while Wyatt play slacker country rock. Over in the US, where there’s always going to be more of this sort of thing, you can point to the current indie-rock holy trinity of Waxahatchee , Wednesday and MJ Lenderman , plus Florry, Ratboys, Thomas Dollbaum, Fust, SG Goodman, Lily Seabird, Ryan Davis and the Roadhouse Band and more. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Get up, get breakfast, noise’: the teen going viral for enduring all 400 of Merzbow’s ear-splitting albums
data.description: The infamous Japanese noise artist has a vast and forbidding catalogue that commands a cult fandom. Sam Andrews, 18, is vlogging his way through the lot – and taking a stand for deep listening An Instagram Reel that looks like an 80s coming-of-age movie pops up on your feed. It’s four teenage boys in an American-style basement – comfy sofas, guitars, ping pong table – jeering and laughing. But they aren’t secretly drinking beer or planning on sneaking out. They’re brandishing a vinyl copy of Pulse Demon , the most popular album from the cult Japanese noise artist Merzbow, and subjecting themselves to its brutally harsh sound in full, for fun. “I think this is the Book of Revelation: The Soundtrack,” one guy blurts out, a vague look of fear in his eyes. Merzbow, real name Masami Akita, is the world’s most renowned noise artist. Since 1979, Akita has released more than 400 recordings, which range from a 10-hour long album misleadingly titled Merzbient (it’s anything but ambient) to a free-noise supergroup called Flying Testicle. Since February, Sam Andrews, the video’s 18-year-old creator, has been attempting to listen to every one, and is documenting his progress online each day. “I think of my day in album-size chunks,” he says, laughing. “It’s like, get up at seven, get breakfast and then headphones in: noise.” Continue reading...

data.title: Profits, Prophets, Coaches and Kings by Jared Diamond review – how to change the course of history
data.description: The author of Guns, Germs and Steels falters in this flawed study of whether individuals really make a difference Early in this book, Jared Diamond proudly introduces “what I term ‘the Hamlet test’”, which helps decide whether prominent individuals really make a difference, or whether others might have done just as well. Among William Shakespeare’s contemporaries on the Elizabethan stage, he explains, were “Ben Jonson, Christopher Marlowe and John Webster. But not even their best plays remotely approach in quality Hamlet and Shakespeare’s other masterpieces.” It follows, for Diamond, that Shakespeare was indeed “uniquely talented”: “We can be confident that no Elizabethan other than Shakespeare could have written a masterpiece like Hamlet if Shakespeare hadn’t done so.” One obvious problem with this is that Marlowe was stabbed to death in a pub in Deptford in 1593 at the age of 29, having already written the absolute bangers Doctor Faustus and Tamburlaine, as well as – so it is now thought – co-writing the Henry VI trilogy with the up-and-coming Shakespeare. Shakespeare himself did not begin to compose his major tragedies, including Hamlet, until he was a decade older. So we can’t rule out the possibility that, had Marlowe lived another 10 years, he would have matched or even exceeded his colleague’s genius. Scholars widely agree that Hamlet and Shakespeare’s other masterpieces were possible only thanks to the outsized influence of Marlowe. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘I feel like I’m grieving’: staff on the devastating fallout of widespread layoffs at Xbox
data.description: Last month, Microsoft’s gaming division told its workforce it was cutting 3,200 jobs, which some say will have big ramifications for game development – as well as taking a huge personal toll On the morning of 6 July, an email went out from Asha Sharma, the chief executive of Xbox, to all of the division’s employees around the world. Under the headline “ Resetting Xbox ”, it announced the most significant restructuring in the history of Microsoft’s console business: 3,200 staff would be laid off throughout the financial year to 2027, and 1,600 of those roles would be eliminated immediately. An hour later, at studios throughout company, the Teams meeting invites started arriving. “It was a virtual call with our studio manager,” says Anne Barrett, who was laid off from Bethesda Game Studios Austin. “All of our cameras and microphones were turned off so we weren’t able to say anything or react to anything. We were just brought in, told the news and it was like: ‘You guys are going to lose access to your Slack channel.’ So you saw a flurry of goodbye messages before everything was just shut off.” Continue reading...

data.description: South African artist Puleng Mongale explores how her childhood church still connects her to the women of her family, not through religion but shared history and memory This image, called Holy Gang, combines an image of a church in my mother’s home town, Fateng-tse-Ntsho, in Free State province, South Africa, with self-portraits of me, multiplied to form a group of women. Although at first glance the women are moving towards the church, it is not the final destination. Positioned higher, beyond the church, is what appears to be a rising sun. For me, the sun represents a place where I can meet and be with my ancestors beyond religious limitations, even though they were members of the church and I am not. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Not just Hollywood crap’: Mike Leigh on the East End communist who brought world cinema to the UK
data.description: A new season celebrates Contemporary Films and its founder Charles Cooper, who bet on Britain taking to Ingmar Bergman, Yasujiro Ozu, Satyajit Ray – and a young Mike Leigh Occasionally, vital pieces of the cultural jigsaw disappear without anyone really noticing. This, sadly, was the fate of Contemporary Films, the British film distributor that popularised sophisticated, grownup international cinema – foreign language mostly – in the UK, and heralded the arrival of the auteur generation with directors such as Ingmar Bergman, Satyajit Ray, Andrzej Wajda and Yasujiro Ozu. Contemporary, and its founder Charles Cooper, weren’t the only game in town – Kenneth Rive’s Gala was a fellow traveller – but Contemporary got there first, setting up shop in 1951, first with short films for the then popular film society sector, and moving into features with the 1952 Japanese film Children of Hiroshima . Its marketplace clout faded rapidly in the early 1990s, when it was a victim of changing industry practices. But amazingly, the company is still with us – and is planning a 75th anniversary series of screenings to showcase its history. Continue reading...

data.title: Whisky galore – and now plenty more besides: exploring the Scottish island of Islay
data.description: Distilleries are the backbone of Islay’s economy and tourist trade. Thanks to their success, other businesses – from breweries and farms to restaurants and chocolatiers – are now thriving and adding to the island’s appeal The Paps of Jura disappear into the mist as I pedal along the shores of Loch Indaal, and the rain cloud I’ve been racing finally catches up. I stash my hire bike at Port Charlotte youth hostel , quickly change and make it to Lochindaal Seafood Kitchen just before the downpour. I’m soon warmed, by the welcome then by a bowl of creamy fish chowder. “We’ve plenty of fresh seafood just in,” is all the temptation I need to order the seafood plate. It’s a bowl for one, but a hungry one, and soon I’m picking and cracking my way through piles of fat langoustines and crab claws, with hot whisky-butter scallops and plenty of bread and butter. data.title: Smart ideas for preserving summer fruit | Kitchen aide
data.description: From fermenting plums in honey and pickling courgettes in vinegar brine to a British take on kimchi, there are many ways to make the most of the warm-weather harvest What’s the best way to preserve late-summer fruit and veg? Jess, by email Fruit, fruit everywhere, so try fermenting it in honey, says Rachel de Thample, author of The Fermentation Year (published in September). “I’m currently looking at a jar of blackberries, but whole plums would be gorgeous, too,” she says, especially when eaten with blue cheese – “or any cheese, really” – meat or fish; you can also use the syrup like maple syrup or cordial. De Thample packs the fruit into sterilised jars and pours in just enough honey to cover it: “If the fruit has a low acidity, add a spoonful of lemon juice or a splash of cider vinegar as well.” Pop on the lid and leave for a few weeks. “It gets fizzy, but it doesn’t get to that explosive stage, because it has quite a concentrated sugar content. It’ll keep for up to a year at room temperature, but I normally pop it in the fridge after a few weeks.” Kimchi is another option to keep Jess enjoying summer fruits all year round. “In Korea, apples and pears are traditional, but there’s a kimchi for every season and region,” says De Thample, who takes a British approach with a courgette, blackcurrant and strawberry number: “You can use up tomatoes in the paste, too.” Otherwise, if you have plums and damsons, take inspiration from Japanese umeboshi: “That has a high percentage of salt – I use 15% per 100g fruit. Layer the salt and plums in jars and, if it’s really dry, pour over water; otherwise, just crush a couple of the plums so their juices create a brine with the salt.” The brine can then be used like a plummy soy sauce, De Thample says: “Having a few jars stored away always makes me feel like I’m winning.” Damsons are also a dream in flavoured liquors, says Kenji Morimoto, regular Guardian contributor and author of Ferment : “That’s a really nice way to capture their flavour, and all you need is vodka, the fruit and rock [or granulated] sugar. Got a culinary dilemma? Email feast@theguardian.com Continue reading...

data.title: Burnham blames Brexit and Thatcher for ‘wrong turns’ in first Commons speech as PM
data.description: The prime minister said Britain needed to be brutally honest about the mistakes of the last 40 years of UK politics Andy Burnham has blamed Brexit and Margaret Thatcher for a decade of low growth in the UK, arguing that Britain needs to be brutally honest about having taken “a series of wrong turns” in the last 40 years. In his first Commons appearance since he took over as prime minister about six weeks ago, Burnham told MPs he wanted to build a new sense of optimism so “we can make this next decade better than the last”. Hinted that he would commit to spending 3% of GDP on defence by 2030, saying he had appointed John Healey as his chancellor “precisely because” of his position on military spending . Signalled he is open to renationalising the water industry – saying he is looking at “all possible solutions”, as the sector is a “leaking monument” to the failures of privatisation. Opened the door to looking again at electoral reform in Labour’s next manifesto. “I do believe there needs to be a mandate to make that change. There are different views in this house, but I believe we will need to get a consensus at the next election. And if there is that consensus, then a change can be made in the next parliament.” Announced he would attend the Cop31 climate summit in Turkey and continue pursuing green energy – but that he would be “pragmatic” on supply, amid expectations he will approve the Jackdaw gasfield. “The mistake is saying it’s got to be one or the other for political purposes. The truth is, it’s going to have to be both.” Continue reading...

data.title: Germany blames Russia for drone attack at Leipzig airport
data.description: Government says ‘dangerous behaviour’ is part of effort by Moscow to cause damage with hybrid attacks The German government has blamed Russia for the drone attack on Leipzig airport last month, calling it “dangerous behaviour” and part of a systematic and concerted effort by Moscow to “cause great damage” through a large number of hybrid attacks. The interior minister, Alexander Dobrindt, and the foreign minister, Johann Wadephul, ended weeks of speculation and the government’s hesitancy to blame Russia, saying in a brisk 10-minute briefing in Berlin that all indications were the Russian state had provided the knowhow and equipment for the planned attack and “low-level agents” were recruited to carry it out. Continue reading...

data.description: The Global FinPrint initiative explored the health of reefs in 58 countries through underwater cameras, discovering that almost one-fifth of these reefs lacked sharks. This alarming reduction is tied to the closeness of markets and the density of human populations. Nonetheless, areas with conservation efforts, including protected areas and fishing restrictions, exhibited greater shark numbers, emphasizing the importance of sharks for food security and the integrity of marine ecosystems.

data.title: Zombie fungus uses dead female flies to infect healthy flies using spores
data.description: A fungus launches infectious spores using pressurized liquid bursts from dead flies. data.title: En Belgique, les brasseurs en croisade contre le nouveau slogan de prévention contre l’alcool

data.title: Atlético busca virada, elimina o Cruzeiro e avança à semifinal da Copa do Brasil

data.title: O fator Augusto Cury
data.description: A surpresa despontou durante o debate da Band, na noite de 23 de agosto : o médico e escritor Augusto Cury era o campeão de buscas na internet. Augusto de quê? Passou-se uma semana e a surpresa encorpou. As pesquisas BTG/Nexus e AtlasIntel/Bloomberg colocaram-no à frente de todos os aspirantes à terceira via. Cury saiu do nada e conseguiu 8% na do BTG e 7,8% na do AtlasIntel. É uma mixaria, já que Lula tem 37% e Flávio Bolsonaro tem 30%. Na pesquisa estimulada, quando o entrevistado recebe um cartão com os nomes dos candidatos, marcou 11%, contra 2% da pesquisa anterior . Continua sendo uma mixaria. Não é mixaria o fato de ele ter pulado de 8,3 milhões de seguidores para 10,5 milhões em menos de uma semana, um dos maiores incrementos do mundo. Leia mais (09/01/2026 - 23h00)

data.title: Susza uderza w Europę. Część gruntów może przestać nadawać się do upraw
data.description: Postępujące susze, upały i niedobory wody mogą w przyszłości sprawić, że część terenów rolniczych w Europie, szczególnie w najbardziej suchych regionach basenu Morza Śródziemnego, przestanie nadawać się do upraw - ostrzegła dyrektor Europejskiej Agencji Środowiska (EEA) Leena Yla-Mononen w wywiadzie udzielonym European Newsroom (ENR).

data.description: Na złomowisku w Hrubieszowie doszło do niezwykłego odkrycia. Mężczyzna, który szukał części do samochodów, przez przypadek trafił na zabytek archeologiczny. Był to fragment okucia tarczy z II wieku. Co więcej, w środku zachowały się przepalone ludzkie kości.

data.title: Letadlovka Abraham Lincoln zakotvila v Thajsku.  Pattaya zakročila proti prostitutkám
data.description: Americká letadlová loď USS Abraham Lincoln se po více než devíti měsících na moři, během nichž čelila kritice kvůli zhoršujícím se podmínkám na palubě, ve středu přiblížila k přístavu Laem Chabang nedaleko letoviska Pattaya. "K zajištění bezpečnosti a poskytnutí potřebné pomoci bude nasazeno asi 600 příslušníků bezpečnostních složek," sdělil Narit Niramajvong, guvernér provincie Chonburi.

data.title: Sabotáž v Německu odpojila elektrárny. Napětí mezi Berlínem a Moskvou eskaluje
data.description: V rozvodně na západě Německa někdo v úterý večer úmyslně způsobil zkrat. Ten odpojil ze sítě pět bloků elektráren v okolí. Týž den ráno neznámí pachatelé zaútočili na rozvodnu na východě země. Tento případ policie již vyšetřuje jako sabotáž. V Augsburgu výbuch neznámého předmětu zranil několik lidí. Německo z předchozích „hybridních“ útoků obvinilo Rusko, to slibuje odpověď.

data.title: Výbuch u nádraží v Augsburgu zranil dva lidi, Německo řeší i další sabotáže
data.description: Dva lidé utrpěli lehká zranění při výbuchu dosud neznámého předmětu v průchodu budovy nedaleko hlavního vlakového nádraží v jihoněmeckém Augsburgu. Tísňové volání přijala policie v 3:15 ráno. Policie ráno nádraží uzavřela, při vyšetřování nalezla v nedaleké pasáži nalezla podezřelý předmět. Nešlo o výbušninu, provoz byl následně opět obnoven.

data.title: Volby 2026: Televize i ČRo startují předvolební maraton, ten vyvrcholí volebními studii
data.description: Česko čekají v říjnu komunální a senátní volby. Veřejnoprávní i obě největší komerční televize už rozběhly předvolební vysílání. Diváci se mohou těšit na předvolební debaty z velkých měst i menších obcí, rozhovory s kandidáty či duely senátorských kandidátů před druhým kolem hlasování. Od září spustil předvolební vysílání i Český rozhlas. Vrcholem volebních servisů budou v den hlasování volební studia.

data.title: „Jsem jeho ruce i nohy.“ Maxík se narodil bez všech končetin, rodina shání miliony
data.description: „Takový případ vidíme jednou za život,“ slyšeli rodiče dnes ročního Maxíka, který se narodil bez rukou a nohou. Šancí na samostatnost mu mohou být bionické ruce z Rakouska. Pojišťovny na ně však nepřispějí a nadějí na získání 6,4 milionu je tak pouze veřejná sbírka. Maminka dítěte boj nevzdává a redakci iDNES.cz popsala úskalí náročné péče.

data.title: Letní prázdniny 2027 budou krátké: Kdy přesně začínají a kdy končí
data.description: Na školáky čekají v roce 2027 nejkratší prázdniny za posledních pět let, délku „bez přídavků“ zapříčiní hlavně chybějící víkendové přesahy. Žáci do školy půjdou naposledy ve středu 30. června 2027. Do lavic se pak vrátí hned 1. září, které připadá rovněž na středu.

data.title: Policie v Lánech exhumuje ostatky někdejšího ministra zahraničí Masaryka
data.description: Policejní odborníci ve středu exhumují ostatky někdejšího ministra zahraničí Jana Masaryka z rodinné hrobky na hřbitově v Lánech na Kladensku. data.title: Školy přecházejí na „podzemní vyučování“. Rusové pálí a ukrajinské děti se učí v krytu
data.description: Za zvuku sirén, v omezeném režimu či bez obvyklých slavností a rovnou v krytu. Tak v pondělí zahájila nový školní rok velká část školáků v ukrajinské metropoli Kyjevě. Do podzemí je zahnaly neutuchající letecké poplachy kvůli ruským útokům na hlavní město. Školy se tu teď chystají přejít kompletně na „podzemní vyučování“, distanční výuku online nebo kombinace obojího.

data.title: Pavel přijme Plagu kvůli rozpočtu. Školství je priorita, kritizoval návrh prezident
data.description: Prezident Petr Pavel ve středu krátce po poledni na Pražském hradě přijme ministra školství Roberta Plagu ( ANO). Jedním z hlavních témat bude rozpočet resortu, v němž podle ministra stále chybí šest miliard korun. Pavel v úterý zdůraznil, že vzdělávání považuje za jednu ze strategických priorit Česka a stát by to měl ukázat i v penězích.

data.title: Cisterna s hořlavou látkou se převrátila do příkopu. Policie evakuovala továrnu
data.description: Cisterna s hořlavou látkou havarovala v úterý odpoledne na silnici I/10 mezi Veseckem a Turnovem na Semilsku. Policisté společně s hasiči evakuovali blízkou továrnu. Úsek mezi kruhovým objezdem u firmy Ontex a od Turnova sjezdem ze silnice I/35 byl zcela uzavřený. Cisterna zřejmě převážela bionaftu, uvedli hasiči na síti X. Provoz se podařilo obnovit ve 3:40 hodin. Úsek je již plně průjezdný.

data.title: Hnutí ANO chce v Ostravě zpět primátora, lídrem Vereš. O senát bojuje Vilamová
data.description: S takřka maximálními cíli vstoupilo do předvolební kampaně v Ostravě hnutí ANO. data.title: Na selhání srdce umírají lidé zbytečně. Pomoc existuje, říká profesor Netuka
data.description: Čechy drtí epidemie srdečního selhání. Když nezabírají léky, pacienti, jejichž srdce nestíhá přečerpávat krev, potřebují nový „motor“. Ne vždy je ale možná transplantace srdce od dárce. Loni zemřelo přímo na selhání srdce 7,3 tisíce lidí. „Někteří zbytečně. Umíme pomoci i jinak, ale jen pokud se k nám pacienti dostanou včas,“ líčí kardiochirurg Ivan Netuka.

data.title: Žijeme si líp, než kolik jsme ochotni zaplatit na daních, varuje ekonom
data.description: Ministryně financí Alena Schillerová předložila vládě státní rozpočet na příští rok se schodkem 389 miliard korun, podle ekonomů je problém, že čisté investice tvoří jen velmi malou část rozpočtu. „Česko si zvyklo málo investovat a přehazovat provozní náklady na příští generace. Pokud si tento zvyk udržíme dost dlouho, může stát zamířit k bankrotu,“ říká v rozhovoru pro iDNES.cz ekonom České spořitelny a předseda Výboru pro rozpočtové prognózy Michal Skořepa.

data.title: Kaple jako rodinný dům. V Praze je na prodej unikátní nemovitost
data.description: Bydlet na zámku už dnes není nic neobvyklého. Někteří si však za svůj domov volí i církevní stavby. V Praze je nyní na prodej kaple z 18. století přestavěná na rodinný dům. Netypický dvoupodlažní dům s užitnou plochou 276 metrů čtverečních, sklepem a velkou zahradou se nachází vedle kláštera benediktinek Venio nedaleko obory Hvězda.

data.title: Poplatky nejspíš skončí o rok později. Nacher o ČT i změnách na stadionech
data.description: Avizované zrušení koncesionářských poplatků ČT a rozhlasu nabírá zpoždění. Místopředseda Sněmovny Patrik Nacher (ANO) v rozhovoru pro Rozstřel na iDNES.cz jako první z koalice připouští, že k němu nejspíš dojde až od roku 2028. „Pokud to nestihneme k 1. lednu 2027, logika velí, aby se to posunulo na 1. ledna 2028 i přesto, že by byl zákon připravený třeba už v březnu,“ říká Nacher.

data.title: Zelenskyj varoval aerolinky před drony v Rusku. Státní terorismus, ohradil se Putin
data.description: Ukrajinský prezident Volodymyr Zelenskyj varoval letecké dopravce a pojišťovny před využíváním ruského vzdušného prostoru. Na nebi zamořeném drony podle něj není místo pro civilní letectví. Ruský prezident Vladimir Putin, který se v Kyrgyzstánu účastní summitu Šanghajské organizace pro spolupráci (SCO) na Zelenského slova uvedl, že je neslyšel, ale že znějí jako státní terorismus.

data.title: Reportagem. Fações armadas condicionam voto e infiltram-se na política do Rio de Janeiro
data.description: A coação armada exercida por milícias e pelo narcotráfico está a forçar a desativação e transferência de secções eleitorais na Região Metropolitana do Rio de Janeiro. A Justiça Eleitoral determinou a mudança de 66 secções de voto das eleições de 4 de outubro devido ao crime organizado. A medida abrange 188 mil eleitores de 20 municípios, mais 13 do que em 2024.

data.title: EU official says it’s not time to ‘normalize’ Russia at G20 finance talks
data.description:
ASHEVILLE: EU economy chief Valdis Dombrovskis said Tuesday that it is not the time to “normalize” Moscow’s presence at G20 meetings as European leaders pushed back against the Russian finance minister’s attendance at ongoing talks.
	“I think the European position is known,” Dombrovskis told reporters on the sidelines of the US-hosted finance leaders’ gathering in Asheville, North Carolina.
	“We do not think now is the time to normalize Russia” or its presence at such talks, the Latvian official said.

data.title: Israeli strikes in Gaza kill three in operation to seize Hamas figure: officials
data.description:
GAZA CITY, Palestinian Territories: Heavy Israeli bombardment killed three people in Gaza City on Tuesday, Palestinian health officials said, in what both sides described as an Israeli-backed ground operation to seize a senior Hamas figure.

	Eyewitnesses reported around a dozen strikes on Tuesday morning in western Gaza City, where the territory’s civil defense agency said three people were killed, including two children and a woman.

data.title: ‘Massive’ Russian missile, drone attack on Kyiv kills 8
data.description:
KYIV: A “massive” Russian attack killed at least eight people in Kyiv overnight, including seven at a railways depot, officials said Tuesday, as Moscow pressed its air campaign on the Ukrainian capital and surrounding areas.
	The strikes came as children were set to return to school after summer holidays and as authorities tightened security measures following weeks of intensified Russian attacks on the capital.

data.title: World leaders need to see rising oceans in Pacific: UN official
data.description:
KOROR: Leaders from the world's top economies should stand on a Pacific atoll to see the reality of record sea level rise, a top UN official said in Palau on Monday.

	Noting last week's deadly floods in Nepal, United Nations Deputy Secretary-General Amina Mohammed said rising seas in the Pacific were the "other side of that story".

	"We do already know that a warming climate is changing the world's ice at extraordinary speeds, not only threatening the communities below glaciers but adding more water to our oceans," she told reporters.

data.title: Iran president says Tehran would ‘immediately’ reciprocate if US returns to June deal
data.description:
Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan: Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian said Tuesday that Tehran would "immediately" reciprocate if the United States returned to a June deal aimed at ending their war.
	"I state explicitly that if the United States returns to its commitments under the aforementioned memorandum of understanding, the Islamic Republic of Iran will immediately take reciprocal action," Pezeshkian said at a Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Kyrgyzstan, according to the website of the Iranian presidency.

data.title: California lawmakers pass bill allowing people to identify their Jewish ancestry on state forms
data.description:
SACRAMENTO, California: California would allow Jews to voluntarily identify their Jewish heritage on state forms under a bill the state Legislature passed Monday.
	The bill, which lawmakers sent to Gov. Gavin Newsom’s desk, would require state agencies that collect demographic information to add “Jewish” as an option for ethnicity or ancestry. The goal is to give state officials and researchers better data on Jewish Californians, including their unemployment rates and representation in schools.

data.title: Nepal says death toll rises to 987, bringing total killed past 1,000
data.description:
KATMANDU, Nepal: Devastating floods on the China-Nepal border have killed at least 987 people in Nepal, the disaster authority said Tuesday, taking overall deaths to more than 1,000.

	Chinese state media earlier confirmed 16 people were killed in Tibet, bringing the total toll from Wednesday’s disaster to 1,003.

	The number of missing in Nepal dropped to 3,916, as rescue efforts entered a seventh day, and the bodies recovered rose.

	In China, state media say there 546 people missing, taking the overall number of missing to 4,462.

data.title: Lebanon urges Greece to help implement deal with Israel
data.description:
ATHENS: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun asked Greece on Monday for support in implementing a US-sponsored agreement with Israel, hours after Greece and Israel announced a multibillion-dollar arms deal.

	Israel and Lebanon launched direct talks aimed at ending hostilities after Iran-backed Hezbollah drew Lebanon into the Middle East war in March by attacking Israel, which responded with massive strikes and a ground invasion.

data.title: Junta Monetaria ajusta proyección del precio del petróleo y qué se prevé con la inflación

En este escenario, la inflación cerraría el año en 3.75%.

data.title: Trésor Mossi : L’Émissaire des Collines tenterait les Aigles
data.description:
Sous la voûte indigo du crépuscule de Bujumbura, un murmure a traversé les travées rutilantes du Stade Intwari. Et a fait irruption. 
 Trésor Mossi s’est présenté. 
 Déjà auréolé du maillot des Intamba mu Rugamba, le stratège de 25 ans a foulé la pelouse des Aigles Noirs, non en visiteur, mais en prétendant. Au menu de cette séance : forger l’acier nécessaire pour affronter un géant, Al Hilal du Soudan, exilé paradoxal du Nil qui dispute désormais son football dans l’arène de la Rwanda Premier League.

Le transfert est tombé comme une estocade. 
Bigirimana Abedi,  milieu offensif et international burundais, quitte Rayon Sports du Rwanda pour poser ses crampons à Damas. Direction : Al-Jaish SC. 
 Après de longues négociations, l’enfant du Burundi rejoint le monument du football syrien.

data.title: Monseigneur Ruhuna Joachim : l’évêque-bâtisseur au cœur de velours
data.description:
Sous la coupole d’un ciel burundais, à Ruyigi, s’est éteinte une lumière. Mais les échos de son pas résonnent encore dans les couloirs de pierre, dans les cours d’écoles, dans les nefs des églises qu’il a fait surgir de la terre rouge.  
 Monseigneur Ruhuna Joachim n’était pas un prélat de chancellerie. C’était un homme d’une trempe granitique et d’une mansuétude infinie .

data.title: Chronique sur les messages de haine : Les médias, une arme à double tranchant
data.description: Sur la colline Ngara, en commune Mwaro, les témoignages des habitants traduisent une même préoccupation : dans une société marquée par les blessures du passé, les mots peuvent soit rapprocher les communautés, soit raviver les divisions. Ils considèrent qu’un média qui propage les messages de haine n’a pas de place.

data.title: Région Centre/Gitega : Des agriculteurs angoissés face au silence autour des engrais Fomi
data.description: Pendant que la saison culturale bat son plein, la colère et le désarroi s'emparent du monde agricole. Les cultivateurs n’ont aucune information officielle sur la disponibilté des engrais organo-minéraux. Entre  retard des engrais  et compostières de dernière minute, le spectre d'une chute importante des rendements plane sur toutes les collines de Gitega.

data.title: Du combat individuel à la force collective pour une gouvernance locale inclusive
data.description: La province de Buhumuza, unique province du Burundi dirigée par une femme a abrité la 6ᵉ session des Débats-Café sur le leadership politique féminin et la gouvernance locale inclusive organisée par l’Institut néerlandais pour la Démocratie multipartite (NIMD). C’est dans le cadre du projet Arpog, mis en œuvre par NIMD en consortium avec l’Afrabu ainsi que d’autres partenaires sous subvention à des tiers. Le soutien financier est assuré par l’Union européenne.  L’objectif est de renforcer les femmes leaders pour qu’elles puissent conquérir leur place au sein des instances de décision locales sans attendre d’être coptées.

data.title: D’autres incendies, d’autres cœurs brisés
data.description: En l’espace de quatre jours, trois incendies viennent de se produire à Bujumbura, la capitale économique. Deux galeries au centre-ville ont été totalement ravagés tandis qu’au sud, une partie du marché est partie en fumée. Les victimes ne savent plus à quel saint se vouer. Des officiels ne tiennent pas le même langage. Des observateurs appellent aux enquêtes pour établir les responsabilités.

data.title: Primus Ligue : La 3ème journée ou le cantique inaugural des ambitions
data.description: Après trois actes, le rideau se lève sur une hiérarchie qui commence à se dessiner en filigrane. La Primus Ligue 2026-2027, dans sa prime jeunesse, offre déjà le spectacle d’un échiquier où chaque pion, chaque cavalier, chaque roi cherche à imposer sa loi. Le classement, implacable et sibyllin, nous livre ses premières vérités.

data.title: Patrimoine vivant : la jeunesse camerounaise réinvente la tradition à l’UNESCO
data.description: © DR Le 28 août 2026, le Bureau régional de l'UNESCO pour l'Afrique centrale a accueilli une activité de Min'art & AMIS, réunissant des jeunes autour de la confection de tenues, de bijoux et de savoir-faire locaux au service des Industries Culturelles et Créatives. Le patrimoine ne se conserve pas seulement. Il se transmet, se porte, se façonne et se réinvente. C’est autour de cette conviction que le Bureau régional de l’UNESCO pour l’Afrique centrale a accueilli, le 28 août dernier, une activité portée par Min’art & AMIS (Ancestral Moves Institute Summit), réunissant des jeunes autour du patrimoine culturel camerounais. Au programme : échanges intergénérationnels, confection de tenues et de bijoux traditionnels, et valorisation des savoir-faire locaux. Une immersion concrète qui a créé un espace vivant de transmission entre culture, jeunesse et création. Au-delà de l’atelier, la rencontre a mis en lumière le potentiel économique et créatif de ces pratiques pour les Industries Culturelles et Créatives au Cameroun. Une façon de transformer l’héritage ancestral en levier d’innovation, d’emploi et d’identité. Une initiative qui rappelle que la culture, portée par la jeunesse, reste un moteur de résilience et de fierté. Cet article Patrimoine vivant : la jeunesse camerounaise réinvente la tradition à l’UNESCO est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Cameroun : 252 800 nouveaux électeurs inscrits sur les listes électorales en 2026
data.description: © DR Élections Cameroon, par la voix du directeur général des élections, Erik Essousse, a fait le point de la campagne de révision des listes électorales mardi dernier au siège d’Elecam à Yaoundé, au lendemain de la clôture des opérations. La campagne de révision des listes électorales lancée le 02 janvier 2026 a pris fin le lundi 31 août dernier. Au terme des opérations d'enrôlement, 252 830 nouveaux électeurs se sont fait enregistrer au cours de la période dédiée, dont 150 954 hommes, 101 876 femmes, 169 225 jeunes (dont 103 230 jeunes hommes et 65 995 jeunes femmes), et 176 personnes vivant avec un handicap. La proportion des électeurs enregistrés dans la diaspora est de 234 personnes dont 150 hommes et 84 femmes. Au cours de la campagne, les services d'Elections Cameroon ont effectué 39 681 mises à jour, 803 modifications, 14 362 transferts et 24 516 radiations. Les équipes ont aussi procédé à la distribution des cartes électorales. Entre janvier et fin août 2026, 102 894 cartes d'électeurs ont été distribuées sur les 887 910 cartes restantes au 31 décembre 2025. Soit un taux de distribution de 11,58%. Les chiffres à propos des nouvelles inscriptions varient d'une région à une autre. La région du Centre est en tête avec 37 595 nouveaux électeurs, soit 14,86%. L'Extrême-Nord est deuxième avec 34 924 nouveaux électeurs. Au troisième rang se trouve le Nord-Ouest avec 32 869 nouveaux inscrits. Le Littoral suit avec 28 320 nouveaux électeurs tandis que le Sud-Ouest occupe le cinquième rang avec 28 112 nouveaux inscrits sur les listes électorales. À présent, le fichier électoral national non toiletté contient 8 238 778 électeurs. La révision des listes étant terminée, Élections Cameroon va entamer les opérations de toilettages du fichier électoral en conformité avec les articles 78 et 80 du Code électoral. Au terme de ces opérations, l'institution publie les listes électorales provisoires au plus tard le 20 octobre et les la liste électorale nationale le 30 décembre. En attendant, la distribution des cartes d'électeurs se poursuit. Les équipes d'Elecam « sillonnent les quartiers en faisant du porte-à-porte et envoyant les SMS aux titulaires de cartes non retirées », a indiqué le directeur général des élections Erik Essousse lors du point de presse donné le 1er septembre. Il invite les personnes dont les cartes sont disponibles à passer les récupérer auprès des déménagements communaux d'Elecam. Cet article Cameroun : 252 800 nouveaux électeurs inscrits sur les listes électorales en 2026 est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Aviation civile : le Cameroun explore la filière des carburants durables
data.description: © DR La CCAA, avec l’OACI et l’appui de l’Union européenne, a lancé le 31 août 2026 une étude de faisabilité sur les carburants d’aviation durables (SAF), dont les conclusions sont attendues dans six mois pour une feuille de route nationale. Le Cameroun se positionne sur l’aviation verte. La Cameroon Civil Aviation Authority (CCAA), en collaboration avec l’Organisation de l’Aviation Civile Internationale (OACI) et avec le soutien de l’Union Européenne, a lancé le 31 août 2026 une étude de faisabilité consacrée aux carburants d’aviation durables (SAF). L’étude vise à évaluer les ressources disponibles, les technologies adaptées et les conditions nécessaires au développement d’une filière nationale de production et d’utilisation des SAF. Elle doit aussi analyser les retombées pour l’économie : création d’emplois, valorisation des ressources locales et réduction des émissions du transport aérien. Le calendrier est établi : après deux jours d’échanges entre experts et parties prenantes, des enquêtes de terrain seront menées pendant dix jours auprès des acteurs industriels, agricoles et des infrastructures concernées. Les conclusions, attendues dans six mois, permettront d’élaborer une feuille de route conforme aux normes de l’OACI. Une étape stratégique pour aligner le transport aérien camerounais sur les engagements climatiques internationaux tout en créant de la valeur locale. Cet article Aviation civile : le Cameroun explore la filière des carburants durables est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: CEMAC : Yaoundé ouvre la mission d’évaluation macroéconomique
data.description: © DR Conduite par Jean Claude Nguemeni, la mission de la Commission de la CEMAC a démarré 1er septembre 2026 à Yaoundé par une concertation au Comité Technique de Suivi des Programmes Économiques présidé par Jean Tchoffo, pour valider l'agenda et cadrer les échanges. Coup d’envoi de la surveillance multilatérale au Cameroun. Ce 1er septembre 2026 a démarré la mission d’évaluation et de cadrage macroéconomique menée par les équipes de la Commission de la Communauté Économique et Monétaire de l’Afrique Centrale (CEMAC), sous la conduite de Monsieur Jean Claude Nguemeni, accompagné du Représentant-Résident et de la Représentante-Adjointe. Mécanisme au cœur de la coordination économique des six États membres à savoir le Cameroun, Centrafrique, Congo, Gabon, Guinée équatoriale et Tchad, la surveillance multilatérale vise à aligner les trajectoires nationales sur les standards communautaires. Trois objectifs prioritaires structurent la mission : assurer la convergence des politiques budgétaires et macroéconomiques pour renforcer la résilience de la zone, garantir la stabilité de la monnaie commune en veillant aux équilibres financiers, et renforcer la discipline budgétaire et la transparence dans la gestion des finances publiques. La concertation tenue ce jour au Comité Technique de Suivi des Programmes Économiques (CTS), présidé par Monsieur Jean Tchoffo, a permis de définir les questions stratégiques à aborder et de valider l’agenda de la mission. Cet article CEMAC : Yaoundé ouvre la mission d’évaluation macroéconomique est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: PROLOG-NASLA : 850 millions pour muscler la décentralisation
data.description: © DR Le PROLOG et la National School of Local Administration ont signé le 31 août 2026 à Yaoundé une convention de 850 millions FCFA sur 12 mois pour former près de 2 000 responsables des CTD de six régions sur la gouvernance locale. La décentralisation passe à la vitesse supérieure. Le Projet Gouvernance Locale et Communautés Résilientes (PROLOG) et la National School of Local Administration (NASLA) ont scellé le 31 août 2026 à Yaoundé une convention de collaboration de près de 850 millions de FCFA pour une durée de douze mois. Objectif : renforcer les capacités des Collectivités Territoriales Décentralisées. Dans les prochains jours, près de 2 000 élus et responsables locaux des régions de l’Extrême-Nord, du Nord, de l’Adamaoua, de l’Est, du Nord-Ouest et du Sud-Ouest bénéficieront de formations ciblées sur la gouvernance financière, la gestion des ressources humaines et l’état civil. L’initiative vise à doter les acteurs locaux de compétences et d’outils pour améliorer la gestion publique locale et la qualité des services rendus aux populations. À travers ce partenariat, PROLOG et NASLA réaffirment leur engagement pour une décentralisation plus efficace, portée par des ressources humaines qualifiées. « Le renforcement des capacités des acteurs des CTDs doit trouver sa traduction concrète dans la qualité des prestations fournies aux populations », a souligné le Ministre de la Décentralisation et du Développement Local. Cet article PROLOG-NASLA : 850 millions pour muscler la décentralisation est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Routes au Cameroun : le programme 2026 sous forte pression
data.description: © DR Sur 155 projets routiers programmés en 2026, seuls 30 achevés au 28 juillet et 70 espérés d’ici décembre, soit 45,2%. Le Mintp recense 57 projets à risque élevé couvrant 205 km de construction, 154 km de réhabilitation et 1 004 ml d’ouvrages d’art. Le compte n’y est pas. La revue à mi-parcours du Ministère des Travaux Publics révèle un important retard dans l’exécution du programme routier 2026. Au 28 juillet 2026, sur les 155 projets dont la livraison était prévue cette année, seulement 30 étaient achevés. Le Mintp estime que 40 autres pourraient être livrés d’ici fin décembre si le rythme se maintient, portant le total à 70 projets, soit 45,2% de la programmation annuelle. Plus préoccupant, 57 projets présentent un risque élevé de non-achèvement, contre 29 à risque faible. Ces 57 opérations concentrent à elles seules 205 km de routes en construction, 154 km en réhabilitation, 66 km en entretien confortatif et 1 004 mètres linéaires d’ouvrages d’art. S’y ajoutent 1 411 km de routes à entretenir avec les sociétés forestières et des études sur 1 029 km et 70 ml d’ouvrages. En cause, selon le Mintp, les retards de paiement, la faible mobilisation des entreprises, des procédures de contractualisation inachevées, la forte pluviométrie et l’insécurité. À fin juin, l’exécution financière restait faible, hypothéquant encore l’atteinte des objectifs. Cet article Routes au Cameroun : le programme 2026 sous forte pression est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Cameroun/ MRC contre Minat : Léon Theiller Onana dénonce l’intervention sélective du Minat dans le fonctionnement des partis
data.description: © DR Le président de l'Organisation du mouvement patriotique se préoccupe d'une certaine « intervention sélective » de l'administration dans le fonctionnement des partis politiques. Le président dudit parti, Léon Theiller Onana fait une comparaison entre le traitement réservé au RDPC et celui des autres partis politiques. L'Organisation du mouvement patriotique sort de son silence. Le parti politique rend publique sa position au sujet de l'échange épistolaire entre le ministre de l'Administration territoriale, Paul Atanga Nji, et le MRC. Le membre du gouvernement qui refuse de reconnaître les résolutions de la convention tenue en décembre 2025. Le Mouvement pour la renaissance du Cameroun qui dénonce la violation de la loi par le ministre. Entre les deux parties, l'OMP se penche du côté du MRC pour dénoncer la posture du ministre. Le parti de Léon Theiller Onana considère cette posture comme « contraire aux exigences de neutralité de l'administration, de l'égalité devant la loi et de pluralisme démocratique ». Alors que le ministre semble s'intéresser de près aux activités du MRC, l'OMP tente de réorienter son attention aussi vers les Rassemblement démocratique du peuple camerounais. Parti dont l’OMP remet en question la légalité de la prorogation de mandats au sein des organes dirigeants, le Comité central et le Bureau politique en l'occurrence. Le conseiller municipal RDPC de la commune de Monatele, Léon Theiller Onana, a attaqué devant le tribunal de grande instance du Mfoundi 02 juillet 2025 les résolutions du Bureau politique du RDPC du 03 novembre 2016. C'était au motif que le mandat des membres dudit Bureau ont pris des résolutions deux mois après la fin de leur mandat en septembre 2016. C'est aussi à ce moment, rappelle Léon Theiller Onana, que le mandat du président Paul Biya à la tête du parti a expiré. Expiration justifiant l'illégalité des prorogations ayant suivi, tel que l'explique l'homme politique. Il insiste en déclarant que le congrès du Rdpc tenu du 15 au 16 septembre 2011 a permis de réélire le président Paul Biya comme président du parti pour un mandat de cinq ans. Mais depuis lors, le congrès ne s'est plus réuni. Les mandats du président national du parti, du comité central, du Bureau politique, du bureau national OFRDPC et du bureau national OJRDPC ont été prorogés à la faveur d'une résolution du Bureau politique tenu le 03 novembre 2016 au palais des Congrès de Yaoundé. Après la saisine de la justice pour la cause, la procédure est « toujours pendante ». À l'approche des élections municipales et législatives, l'OMP soulève de nouveau la question et interpelle le Minat qui « devra s'appesantir sur le cas préoccupant du RDPC ». Dans un communiqué en date du 1er septembre 2026, l'OMP demande à Elecam et au Conseil constitutionnel de rejeter toutes les listes du RDPC présentées sans tenue préalable du congrès légal ; exige des juridictions saisies, une application rigoureuse de la loi. Le parti invite par ailleurs le ministre Paul Atanga Nji à appliquer au RDPC la même vigilance juridique que celle déployée sur les autres formations politiques. Cet article Cameroun/ MRC contre Minat : Léon Theiller Onana dénonce l’intervention sélective du Minat dans le fonctionnement des partis est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .
